id: ml-04
title: Graph isomorphism networks
paper: Xu, Hu, Leskovec & Jegelka, How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks? (GIN) (ICLR 2019; arXiv Oct 2018)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.00826
type: Mechanism
cutoff: 2018-10-01
domain: ml
profile: method-benchmark

## expected_verdict
Mixed. The expressivity theory is supported: message-passing GNNs are at most as powerful as 1-WL, and GIN with injective aggregation attains it. The "state-of-the-art" empirical claim is weakened. The reported numbers are 10-fold validation accuracies (model selection, not assessment). Under a fair protocol, structure-agnostic baselines match or beat GIN on D&D, PROTEINS and ENZYMES, though GIN clearly wins on NCI1 and social datasets.

## I0
Can a graph network match WL expressivity and improve graph classification?

## evidence
- Theory: Lemma 2 (any aggregation-based GNN is at most as powerful as the WL test); Theorem 3 (GNN with injective neighbour aggregation and readout is as powerful as WL); mean/max aggregators (GCN, GraphSAGE) are not injective on multisets.
- GIN update: MLP((1 + ε)·h_v + Σ h_u); GIN-0 fixes ε = 0.
- Data: 9 benchmarks: MUTAG, PTC, NCI1, PROTEINS (bio); COLLAB, IMDB-B, IMDB-M, REDDIT-B, REDDIT-M5K (social, uninformative node features).
- Protocol: 10-fold CV, reporting average validation accuracy across folds (§7); 5 GNN layers, 2-layer MLPs, BatchNorm, Adam lr 0.01 halving every 50 epochs; small hyperparameter grid per dataset.
- Results: GIN fits training data almost perfectly; reports best test accuracy among GNNs on most datasets.

## intake
- Scope: (A) theoretical: expressivity bounds and GIN reaching WL power; (B) empirical: GIN improves graph classification accuracy.
- Regime: standard TU benchmarks, small datasets (MUTAG validation folds ~18 graphs).
- Assumptions for (B): 10-fold validation accuracy estimates generalization; structure contributes to the labels.
- Falsifiers: for (A), a proof error; for (B), structure-agnostic baselines matching GIN under nested CV, or the gain vanishing with proper model assessment.

## screen
- Must flag: expressivity (distinguishing graphs) ≠ generalization; reported numbers mix model selection and evaluation; tiny datasets with high variance.
- Must request: nested CV / held-out assessment; structure-agnostic baselines.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: Weisfeiler–Lehman test and WL subtree kernel (Shervashidze et al. 2011); GCN (Kipf & Welling); GraphSAGE (Hamilton et al.); deep sets / multiset functions (Zaheer et al.); Yanardag & Vishwanathan and Niepert et al. protocols.
- Current mode: Errica et al. 2020: >47,000 experiments, 5 GNNs, 9 datasets, fair model selection; GIN's paper reports validation accuracy of 10-fold CV; on chemical data GIN 80.0 vs baseline 69.8 on NCI1, but baseline ≥ GIN on D&D (78.4 vs 75.3), PROTEINS (75.8 vs 73.3), ENZYMES (65.2 vs 59.6).

## designer
- Check theorem assumptions separately. Empirically: nested CV with inner model selection; structure-agnostic baselines (molecular fingerprints / degree histograms); report variance.

## champion
- Errica et al.'s structure-agnostic MLP baselines (atom counts for chemistry; degree features for social graphs); WL subtree kernel SVM.

## panel
- Accept (A). For (B): flag validation-accuracy reporting; repair with held-out assessment.

## run
- PyG GIN on NCI1 and PROTEINS with nested CV and the structure-agnostic baseline; expect GIN > baseline on NCI1, not on PROTEINS.

## verdict
- Label: Mixed: theory Supported; empirical superiority Limited/conditional.
- Must say: the expressivity theorem stands independently of benchmark margins; margins shrink under fair evaluation and vary by dataset.
- Must not say: GIN is no better than baselines anywhere (NCI1 and social sets show gains); or GIN is SOTA on all benchmarks.

## audit
- Check: Lemma 2 and Theorem 3 statements; "validation accuracies across the 10 folds" quote; Errica Table 3 numbers.

## variants
- Datasets where labels require structural distinctions beyond degree counts (e.g. synthetic WL-distinguishable tasks, or molecular properties dependent on rings).
